interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary: Scotland’s power system is currently operating under exceptionally high renewable penetration, with wind generation reaching a formidable 4.4 GW. This clean dispatch has driven regional carbon intensity down to an impressive 32 gCO2/kWh, positioning the Scottish network as an effective decarbonization engine for the wider British electricity market. However, this production peak exposes acute transmission friction. Real-time telemetry indicates 221.1 MWh of wasted energy, a direct symptom of transmission curtailment resulting from thermal and stability limits across the heavily congested B6 Anglo-Scottish export boundary. While generation output remains exceptionally robust, existing grid infrastructure cannot fully evacuate this localized surplus southwards toward primary national demand centers. This structural bottleneck emphasizes the escalating necessity for targeted capital investment in co-located battery storage assets, dynamic line rating systems, and grid-forming technologies. In the near term, prioritizing localized flexible demand response and accelerating network reinforcement are critical steps to minimizing expensive constraint payments. Until transmission capacity expands to match generation capability, substantial volumes of zero-marginal-cost green power will continue to be discarded, dampening asset profitability and system-wide efficiency.
